questions.question: What is the safest first step after an elevated office blood-pressure reading in a stable patient?
choices: Verify technique and obtain repeated or appropriate out-of-office data
questions.explanation: Confirmation includes technique, repeated readings, context, and appropriate out-of-office data.

questions.question: Which presentation needs emergency evaluation?
choices: Severe BP elevation with chest pain and new dyspnea
A request for a home cuff
questions.explanation: Severe elevation with symptoms suggesting acute target-organ injury needs emergency assessment.

questions.question: Which factor is important in hypertension assessment?
choices: CV/renal risk, medicines, sleep, alcohol, adherence, and access
questions.explanation: Hypertension management is risk- and context-based.

questions.question: Why can apparent treatment failure occur?
choices: Technique, white-coat effect, access, interfering agents, or secondary causes

questions.question: What should medication counseling include?
choices: Purpose, timing, adverse effects, monitoring, and follow-up
questions.explanation: Education and monitoring are part of safe management.

questions.question: When should secondary hypertension prompt consultation?
choices: When pattern or comorbidity suggests an underlying cause

questions.question: Why assess NSAID use?
choices: It may contribute to BP and renal risk

questions.question: What makes a BP plan patient-centered?
choices: Considering comorbidities, access, goals, risks, and monitoring
questions.explanation: Individualized plans are safer and feasible.

questions.question: What closes the follow-up loop?
choices: Named monitoring, follow-up timing, ownership, and escalation precautions

questions.question: What is the core FNP approach?
choices: Manage physiology, risk, barriers, response, and safety
Use emergency care for every reading
questions.explanation: FNP care integrates confirmation, risk, management, and follow-up.
